definitions.explanation: A calendar where one page is torn off each day to reveal the next date. Often features daily quotes, trivia, or seasonal information. Short for 日めくりカレンダー.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{日|ひ}めくりをめくる。
examples.english: I tear off a page of the daily calendar every morning.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}の{家|いえ}には{日|ひ}めくりカレンダーがかかっている。
examples.english: There is a tear-off calendar hanging at my grandmother's house.

examples.japanese: この{日|ひ}めくりには{毎日|まいにち}{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}が{一|ひと}つ{載|の}っていて{勉強|べんきょう}になる。
examples.english: This daily calendar features one four-character idiom each day, which is educational.

notes: From {日|ひ} (day) + めくる (to turn/tear off). Full form is {日|ひ}めくりカレンダー. Still common in Japanese homes, especially among older generations. Popular types include those with {名言|めいげん} (famous quotes), {暦|こよみ} (traditional calendar) information, or {俳句|はいく} (haiku). The verb used for tearing off a page is めくる or はがす.
